title: Protocol for isolation of mouse pre-implantation embryos for gene expression analysis
protocol: Bring the mice to the euthanasia room and perform cervical dislocation to sacrifice the mice.
Spray alcohol on the belly of the mouse and wipe with tissue paper.
Using a tweezer lift up the skin fold and cut open the skin and abdominal lining to expose the uterine horns.
Cut the uterine horn using fine forceps and scissors, placing it in a dish containing 1× PBS at 25°C–28°C.
Take media in a 1 ml syringe and plunge it into the uterine horns while holding them properly with a tweezer to wash out contents into a 4-well dish.
Repeat the process twice for both uterine horns.
Allow the embryos to settle down for 10-15 minutes.
Observe the embryos under a phase contrast microscope.
Wash the embryos twice or thrice with 1× PBS to remove debris.
Transfer the embryos to the wells of a 4-well plate by mouth pipetting.
Take a micrograph with a phase contrast microscope for further reference.
Pool the embryos if isolating them from multiple female mice and sort the embryos for various procedures.
Proceed to fixation step if the embryo is to be used for immunofluorescence.
Perform until the blocking stage.
Store the embryos at 4°C after blocking, or proceed immediately for staining.
Transfer the embryos to a 1.5 mL microfuge tube for RNA isolation.
Immerse the microfuge containing embryos in liquid nitrogen for 2–3 min to snap freeze them.
Store the frozen embryos at -80°C.
Let the embryos settle for 10–15 minutes before visualizing under a microscope.
Use a phase contrast microscope initially to detect embryos.
Record micrographs for each stage of embryonic development.
Fix the embryos with 300 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde in a single well of a 4-well plate.
Incubate the fixed embryos at 25°C–28°C for 10 min.
Wash the embryos thrice with 300 μL of 1× PBS using mouth pipette and in 4-well plate.
Permeabilize the embryo with 300 μL 0.25% TritonX-100.
Incubate permeabilized embryos at 25°C–28°C for 1 h.
Wash the embryos twice with 300 μL 1× PBS.
Incubate the embryos in 300 μL of blocking solution at 25°C–28°C for 2 h or at 4°C for 12–16 h.
Transfer embryos to a microfuge with sufficient volume of blocking solution if storing for prolonged periods.
Dilute primary antibody E-cadherin/CDH1 (1:100) in blocking solution.
Transfer embryos to the diluted antibody solution by mouth pipetting.
Incubate the embryos at 4°C for 12–16 h.
Keep the plate at 25°C–28°C for 10 min the next day.
Wash the embryos thrice with 300 μL of 1× PBS.
Add 200 μL of secondary antibody (1:200, diluted with 1× PBS) and keep for 1 h at 25°C–28°C.
Wash the embryos thrice with 300 μL of 1× PBS, 10 min each.
Add 300 μL of nuclear stain HOECHST (1 mg/mL, diluted in 1× PBS at 1:1000) and keep for 10 min at 25°C–28°C.
Wash the embryos once with 300 μL of 1× PBS for 5 min at 25°C–28°C.
Check the embryos under a fluorescent microscope.
Transfer the embryos to a slide with a cavity.
Mark a small circle on the slide with transparent nail polish.
Add a drop of antifade reagent to the marked area.
Place the coverslip gently over the embryos.
Fix the coverslip by applying transparent nail-polish around its circumference.
Keep the slide at 25°C–28°C for 15–30 min.
Use confocal microscopy to detect E-cadherin/CDH1 presence and localization.
Mix 100 μL of Extraction buffer with the cell pellet by gentle pipetting.
Incubate the samples at 42°C for 30 min in a heating block.
Centrifuge the samples at 3000 × g for 2 min.
Pipette the supernatant containing the extracted RNA into a new microfuge tube.
Condition the RNA purification column by pipetting 250 μL of conditioning buffer onto the filter membrane.
Incubate the column with conditioning buffer for 5 min at 25°C–28°C.
Centrifuge the purification column in the provided collection tube at 16000 × g for 1 minute.
Pipette 100 μL of 70% ethanol to the cell extract.
Mix well by pipetting up and down.
Combine the contents with approximately 200 μL total volume.
Pipette the combined solution into the pre-conditioned purification column.
Centrifuge the samples for 2 minutes at 100 g.
Centrifuge once more at 16000 × g for 30 seconds to remove flow through.
Pipette 100 μL wash buffer 1 into the purification column and centrifuge for 1 minute at 8000 × g.
Pipette 100 μL wash buffer 2 to the purification column and centrifuge for 1 minute at 8000 × g.
Pipette 100 μL wash buffer 2 into the purification column and centrifuge for 2 minutes at 16000 × g.
If any wash buffer remains, centrifuge at 16000 × g for 1 minute.
Transfer the purification column to a new 0.5 mL tube supplied with the kit.
Pipette elution buffer directly onto the membrane of the purification column while gently touching the tip to the surface.
Wait for 3 minutes.
Spin at 8000 × g for 30 seconds.
Discard the column and store the RNA at -80°C.
Wear gloves while conducting the entire procedure.
Isolate RNA from embryos using the Pico-pure kit.
Use at least 20 embryos per stage (4-cell, 8-cell, morula, and blastocyst) for isolating RNA of good quality.
Store isolated RNA at -80°C until ready to use.
Measure the concentration of RNA by Nanodrop.

Prepare the master mix with the cDNA high capacity reverse transcriptase kit as follows: add 10× RT Buffer 2.0 μL, 25× dNTP Mix (100 mM) 0.8 μL, 10× RT Random Primers 2.0 μL, MultiScribe™ Reverse Transcriptase 1.0 μL, RNase Inhibitor 1.0 μL, and Nuclease-free water 3.2 μL to a total volume of 10.0 μL per reaction.
Take at least 50 ng of RNA in a 0.2 mL PCR tube.
Make up the volume to 10 μL with nuclease free water.
Add 10 μL of master mix to the RNA in the PCR tube.
Mix by pipetting once or twice.
Spin the tube for a pulse of 10 s at 800 × g.
Keep the tube on ice until starting the Thermal Cycler.
Initiate PCR cycling conditions: 25°C for 10 min.
Incubate at 37°C for 120 min.
Heat to 85°C for 5 min.
Hold at 4°C.
Store the sample at -20°C.
